requirement:
`habeas coverage-check` MUST check saved execution coverage against
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.threshold` and
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.functions`, returning success only when
every applicable obligation is satisfied or has accepted exception evidence
under {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.exceptions`. The command MUST NOT
build the project, execute tests, collect coverage, or invoke an assessment model.
rationale:
I judged the two `{test}`-marked tests in `tests/execution_coverage.rs` against the obligations that `requirements.test-coverage.check` states itself. The threshold, function and exception rules sit in cited or refining requirements, which have their own tests, so I did not reassess them.

**Obligations in the subject text**
1. `habeas coverage-check` checks saved coverage against the threshold and function rules. It succeeds only when every applicable obligation is met or has accepted exception evidence, and otherwise fails.
2. It MUST NOT build the project.
3. It MUST NOT execute tests.
4. It MUST NOT collect coverage.
5. It MUST NOT invoke an assessment model.

**Test mapping**
- `fn[full_test_flow_checks_real_function_counters_after_all_tests]` covers the pass case for obligation 1.
  - It runs `habeas test`, then the standalone `saved_check` (`habeas coverage-check`).
  - It asserts success and "Coverage check passed" when every function and file is covered.
  - It then rewrites the source so `outer/hidden` has zero execution and reruns. The standalone check fails with "Coverage check failed". The test also asserts that the report names `#fn[outer]/fn[hidden]: zero execution` and does not name `#fn[outer]`. That shows the nested function's lack of execution is reported without the parent being blamed.
  - The recorded test run still has outcome "success", so the failure comes from the coverage policy.
- The same test covers obligation 5. `model_tripwire` configures an authoring backend pointing at a local listener that counts requests. The test asserts zero requests after both `coverage-check` runs.
- It also asserts that the retained `evidence` files are unchanged across the checks.
- `fn[book_rendering_preserves_retained_coverage_and_never_launches_tests]` covers obligations 2–4 and the failure case of 1.
  - It runs `coverage-check` with a `cargo` shim on `PATH`. The shim logs each call and exits 99 for anything other than `metadata`, and the test asserts the forbidden-command marker is never created. That rules out build and coverage-collection commands.
  - A sentinel file is written only if the test body runs. The test asserts the sentinel is absent after the check, so no test was executed.
  - It asserts the retained coverage storage is byte-identical afterwards.
  - It asserts the check fails when functions are unmeasured and prints the "File execution coverage" report.
- The pass, fail and no-side-effect scenarios are each exercised end to end through the real CLI binary.

**Delegated and not assessed here**
- The exact threshold arithmetic and the exception acceptance, staleness and non-transfer rules belong to `requirements.test-coverage.check.threshold`, `.functions` and `.exceptions`. Those are tested in `src/execution_coverage/check.rs#mod[tests]`, for example `exact_per_file_threshold_and_partial_functions` and `accepted_file_and_function_explanations_remain_separate_from_execution`. They are not in scope for this subject.
- No end-to-end CLI test combines an accepted exception with a passing exit code. That exit-code mapping carries no conditional of its own beyond what the CLI tests already assert, and the report-level tests cover the exception logic, so I did not count it as a gap.

I found no requirement-violating behavior that these tests would accept.

text: :::{req} check
`habeas coverage-check` MUST check saved execution coverage against
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.threshold` and
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.functions`, returning success only when
every applicable obligation is satisfied or has accepted exception evidence
under {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.exceptions`. The command MUST NOT
build the project, execute tests, collect coverage, or invoke an assessment model.
:::{req} check.threshold
Each first-party Rust file under
{cite}`requirements.references.rust_item_coverage.parsing` MUST have at least 80%
execution coverage of its instrumented lines, or current accepted exception
evidence explaining why the file falls below that target under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.exceptions`. Counts MUST use the
file-and-line union rule of {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.summary`;
a line counts as executed when any eligible test process or its associated
child processes has a positive execution count for it.
The check MUST use the combined selection and freshness rules of
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.selection` and
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.freshness`, restricted to the active
build configuration. It MUST compare exact counts rather than rounded displayed
percentages, average file percentages, or impose an 80% target within each
function. A file whose executable code is not measured MUST require exception
evidence rather than pass with a fabricated percentage. A file established to
contain no executable coverage obligations MUST be reported as such and MUST
NOT require a threshold exception.
Absence of recorded instrumented lines alone MUST NOT establish that a file
contains no executable coverage obligations.
:::{req} check.functions
Every function under {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.scope` without
recorded execution attributable to it MUST have current accepted exception
evidence under {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.exceptions`, even when
its containing file meets the target of
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.threshold`.
Execution attributable only to another function, including a nested function
or closure, MUST NOT establish coverage of the enclosing function merely
because their source locations overlap. Having no recorded lines alone MUST
NOT establish that a function has no executable coverage obligations.
:::{req} check.exceptions
An unmet file threshold or an unexecuted or not-measured function MAY satisfy
the coverage policy only
through current, accepted, independently assessed evidence explaining why its
coverage is incomplete. An exception MUST be attached to the source file or
function whose incomplete coverage it justifies. A file-threshold exception
MUST NOT automatically excuse untested functions.
An exception MUST NOT excuse another source item's incomplete coverage.
Changes to the source item, justification, or other inputs
of its citation review MUST invalidate the affected exception under
{cite}`requirements.references.citation_review`.
A source comment or unassessed justification alone MUST NOT count as accepted
exception evidence. Function and gap identities MUST remain portable between
equivalent local and CI checkouts rather than depend on checkout paths,
run identifiers, timestamps, or process identifiers.
